description: Kubernetes node drain deadlock caused by PDB and slow pod rescheduling
system_prompt: You are a senior systems engineer with deep expertise in Linux internals, distributed systems, networking, and infrastructure operations. Think through the problem carefully — consider all interacting mechanisms before committing to an answer. Show your reasoning chain explicitly before stating conclusions.
user_message:
A Deployment has 3 replicas spread across 3 nodes (one pod per node: node-1,
node-2, node-3). A PodDisruptionBudget is configured:
  minAvailable: 2

An operator runs: kubectl drain node-1 --ignore-daemonsets

The drain begins: the pod on node-1 is evicted successfully (step 1 completes,
the pod terminates). The evicted pod is rescheduled and lands on node-2, but its
readiness probe has not yet passed — the pod is Running but not Ready.

At this moment, the drain tries to proceed with no further pods to evict from
node-1... but it is now stuck. kubectl drain never completes. No error is printed.

(a) Explain precisely why the drain is stuck. Identify the specific check the
    eviction API performs, what values it sees at this moment, and why it blocks.
    Note: there are no more pods on node-1 to evict — explain what "stuck" means
    in this context if not a pending eviction.

    [Correction for answerers: there IS a second pod being drained — re-read the
    scenario. The operator is draining node-1. After the first pod's eviction, the
    rescheduled pod on node-2 is not yet Ready. What does the eviction API see if
    the drain now attempts to evict a second pod from node-1?]

    Assume node-1 originally had TWO pods (deployment scheduled 2 on node-1, 1 on
    node-2, 0 on node-3 — a skewed initial distribution). The drain successfully
    evicted pod-A. Pod-A is rescheduled to node-3 but not yet Ready. The drain now
    tries to evict pod-B (also on node-1).

(b) Once pod-A becomes Ready on node-3, does the drain automatically unblock and
    complete? Explain the mechanism.
(c) The operator cannot wait. List the options available to unblock the drain
    immediately, in order from least to most disruptive, with the risk of each.
